reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) discusses Mn dissolution and redox buffering in a high-entropy alloy and 316H stainless steel in molten fluoride salt, which is unrelated to the key premises about iron oxide passivation, thickening, and spallation on Q235 carbon steel. No evidence is provided for the room-temperature passivation or high-temperature oxide failure mechanisms specific to Q235.
premises: A thin, adherent Fe2O3/Fe3O4 layer passivates Q235 steel at room temperature.
High-temperature exposure causes oxide film thickening and spallation on Q235 steel.
Thermal stress and oxidation kinetics drive high-temperature oxide failure.
Mn dissolution in molten salts can act as a redox buffer to protect Cr (from E1/E2).
